_role: behavioral-contract — this is the public implementer specification for the User Path Ledger. The machine-verifiable governing-law list lives at data/working/user-path-ledger-spec.json.
name: Agent Buccet User Path Ledger
description: Persistent sub-ledger of the main Agent Buccet ledger. Records all user-originated law decisions made at the action boundary. Authoritative source for NSL pre-checks before presenting user decisions.

userApprovedLawPaths.description: All paths the user has said yes to at the action boundary. Each entry is automatically written as law with status ACTIVE. No second confirmation required.

userDeniedLawPaths.description: All paths the user has explicitly elevated to law via the denial fork. A regular denial does not appear here. Only paths where the user chose 'make denial a law' are stored.

id.description: Unique identifier for this User Path Ledger entry.

type.description: Whether this entry records an approved or denied path.

path.description: Human-readable description of the proposed action path that was decided upon.

pathHash.description: Deterministic hash of the path for efficient NSL lookup. Must be stable across sessions for the same path.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when this law entry was created.

scope.description: SESSION: expires at session end. GLOBAL: persists across all sessions. DOMAIN: applies to a defined category of paths.

status.description: ACTIVE: consulted by NSL. MUTED: not consulted by NSL, entry preserved and reactivatable. DELETED: no longer carries legal force.

witness.description: Reference to the main ledger entry that witnessed this creation or last modification event.

modifiedAt.description: Timestamp of last modification. Null if never modified after creation.

notes.description: Optional user-authored annotation on this entry.

nslLookupContract.description: How NSL queries the User Path Ledger before presenting a decision to the user.
steps: 1. Compute pathHash for the proposed action path.
2. Query User Path Ledger for entries where pathHash matches and status is ACTIVE.
3. If a matching APPROVED entry is found: proceed with the action. Do not ask the user.
4. If a matching DENIED entry is found: block the action as a lawful denial. Do not ask the user.
5. If no matching ACTIVE entry is found: present the decision to the user (yes/no).
6. On yes: write new APPROVED entry to User Approved Law Paths. Entry is ACTIVE immediately.
7. On no: ask exactly once 'Make this denial a law, or regular denial?'
8. On 'make denial a law': write new DENIED entry to User Denied Law Paths. Entry is ACTIVE immediately.
9. On 'regular denial': do not write to ledger. Denial has no future legal force.

view.description: User may view all entries in both sections at any time. No entry is hidden.

modify.description: User may modify any entry (notes, scope). Modification is a witnessed ledger event.

mute.description: User may set any entry to status MUTED. Muted entries are not consulted by NSL. Entry is preserved and reactivatable.

reactivate.description: User may set a MUTED entry back to ACTIVE. Reactivation is a witnessed ledger event.

delete.description: User may delete any entry. Deletion sets status to DELETED and removes the entry from NSL's active lookup. Deletion is a witnessed ledger event.

persistenceRules.SESSION: Entry expires at session end. Not reloaded at next session start.
persistenceRules.GLOBAL: Entry persists across all sessions. Reloaded at session start.
persistenceRules.DOMAIN: Entry persists and applies to all paths matching the defined domain category. Reloaded at session start.
